title: Cross-cluster burst throughput benchmark and regression hunter
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Run a focused cross-cluster burst and sustained throughput benchmark to validate multi-GPU TP/PP scaling and detect regressions introduced by recent kernel-selection and KV cache warmup changes. The goal is to exercise short, high-concurrency bursts (microbursts) and longer steady-state streams across cluster topologies (single-node multi-GPU, multi-node TP-only, combined TP+PP runs) and produce an automated regression-hunter job that: 1) computes tokens/sec and p95 latency per workload slice, 2) flags anomalous regressions vs baselines, and 3) uploads compact artifacts to the perf dashboard for triage.
acceptance_criteria: A repeatable harness that can run end-to-end on CI and on perf-clusters with identical configs
Metrics produced: tokens_per_sec, p95_latency_ms, p50_latency_ms, stderr_rps, GPU_utilization_pct, mem_free_mb
Regression detector produces human-readable diff and raises an alert when tokens/sec drops >7% or p95 increases >15% vs baseline within a window
Artifacts (CSV + screenshot of timing histogram + small KV-warmup profile) uploaded to perf dashboard link
Benchmarks for at least three model sizes (7B, 33B, 70B) across 2, 4, 8 GPU configs and TP/PP combinations completed
Documentation page with runbook and how to add new configs in Confluence
benchmark_matrix: Topology permutations: single-node 2xA100, single-node 4xA100, dual-node 8xA100 (TP-only), 4-node 8xA100 (TP+PP split)
Batch sizes: 1, 4, 16 (with dynamic batching enabled for batch>1 runs)
KV-cache warmup pattern: cold-start, prefix-cached (200 tokens), hybrid (10 short requests then long stream)
Workload profiles: microburst (1000 concurrent rps for 15s), ramp (0->500 rps over 60s), steady-state (sustained 300 rps for 10m)
instrumentation: Driver: burst_driver v0.9 with deterministic request seeds
Telemetry: trace-level token timers (per-token), per-request latency histograms, GPU metrics via node-exporter + nvidia-smi sampling at 1s
Measurement window: warmup 60s (ignored), measurement 300s for steady-state, burst aggregated over 15s windows
Baseline collection: run each config 5 times; baseline = median of runs on baseline-cluster (perf-cluster-1) on 2026-01-20
Noise controls: fixed seed, pinned model versions, isolated network traffic using perf VLANs
anomaly_detection: Pipeline uses two complementary detectors: 1) statistical thresholding comparing median tokens/sec and p95 to baseline with configurable slack (default -7% tokens/sec, +15% p95) and 2) EWMA on tokens/sec with alarm fired when short-term EWMA falls below long-term EWMA by configured margin. When either detector triggers, harness produces a regression bundle (config, raw histograms, 5-run CSV, GPU traces) and posts to perf-slack #perf-regressions and creates a GitHub issue template filled with key metrics.
results_summary: Initial runs (2026-02-18) on 4xA100 single-node: 33B model steady-state tokens/sec=1100 +/- 45 (stdev across runs), p95=22.6ms
Microburst observation: 4xA100 single-node 33B saw transient p95 spikes to 280ms during first 3 bursts due to KV warmup; after pre-warm policy p95 stabilized to 35-45ms
Multi-node TP-only (2 nodes, 8GPUs) showed 8% lower tokens/sec vs single-node aggregate due to extra collectives; matches expected comm overhead in kernel-selection model
TP+PP topology on 4-node split reported 5% higher steady tokens/sec for long sequences (1024) but 12% higher p95 variance for short sequences (64) — likely scheduling jitter between PP stages
Regression detector: flagged a tokens/sec drop of 9% in one 33B TP-only run after kernel selector patch rkp-2026-02-10; regression bundle attached for triage
